title: Shared atoms of the reader contract
description: Referenced by the reader's question and answer, and by core-internal's listing of a public network (DEC-28); validates nothing on its own.

request_id.description: A question's request id: 128 bits Core draws at random for each question, never from a counter, as 32 lower-case hexadecimal characters, its top 64 bits never all zero, which is what a counter written as an id gives (DEC-28's condition (b)).

genesis_hash.description: A Substrate network's genesis hash: 0x and 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

chain_id.description: An EVM network's chain id (EIP-155), in decimal digits with no leading zero, above zero, up to 20 digits.

network_identity.description: A network's identity, which the reader checks before it answers anything and Core holds to the listing: a genesis hash, or a chain id.

depth.description: A count of blocks: at least one.

finality.description: When a movement on the network counts as final (DEC-13): as soon as it is recorded, after a count of confirmations, or once a later checkpoint covers it.

reorg_rule.description: What the network can do to a movement that is not yet final (DEC-13): never undo it, undo it to a depth, or undo it until the finality rule says otherwise.

rpc_endpoint.description: One endpoint of an RPC pool: an https or wss URL to a lower-case DNS name, with an optional port and path, and no user, query or fragment. The reader host's egress reaches it by its name; a key a node needs is resolved by name by the host and never written here.

trust_rule.description: How a reader stands behind what it answers (item reader-answer-trust, DEC-28): an embedded light client (a Substrate network's), or a preset pool of RPC endpoints of which at least the quorum, two or more, must agree (an EVM network's). A pool names each endpoint once and at least as many endpoints as its quorum, which the Rust types check.

quorum.description: How many of the endpoints must agree: at least two.

asked.description: A question, by kind, with what it is about. Each is read-only.

movement.description: The movement asked about, by its id on the network.

transaction.description: The segment's transaction whose movement is asked for.

reason.description: Why a reader can't stand behind an answer, as a token: a label to read, which no decision branches on.
